altText: Ghanaian KG1 children freely exploring straight, curved and zigzag lines plus simple shapes and textures on big sheets of paper.
detailedDescription: In a KG1 classroom, several children sit or stand around low tables covered with large sheets of paper. They experiment with crayons and charcoal sticks to draw straight, curved, zigzag and spiral lines and to make circles, triangles and rectangles. Some place leaves or coins under the paper and rub over them with crayons to discover rough and smooth textures. The teacher moves from group to group asking questions such as 'What kind of line did you make?' and 'How does this feel under the paper?', encouraging free play with tools and materials.

altText: KG1 children mixing red, yellow and blue paints or coloured water to discover new colours and talk about their names.
detailedDescription: At a low art table, KG1 learners wear simple aprons while working with three basic colours: red, yellow and blue. Using brushes or their fingers, they mix small amounts of these colours on thick paper or plastic trays to form orange, green and purple. A simple colour chart hangs nearby showing the names of the primary and mixed colours. The teacher asks 'What colours did you mix to get this?' and helps children say colour names such as red, yellow, blue, orange and green, building both colour vocabulary and awareness of the elements of design.

altText: KG1 children carefully observing and drawing real classroom objects like a cup, shoe and plant placed on a table.
detailedDescription: A small group of KG1 learners sits around a low table where the teacher has placed everyday classroom objects such as a cup, a shoe, a pencil and a small potted plant. Each child has a sheet of paper and a pencil or crayon and is encouraged to look carefully before drawing. As they draw what they see, the teacher prompts them to talk about the objects and the lines and shapes they notice in the environment, helping them connect observation, thinking and simple art vocabulary.

figureLabel: Drawing scenes from home and community
altText: KG1 children drawing scenes from their homes and communities such as families helping and children at school.
detailedDescription: KG1 learners sit on a mat or at small tables creating drawings of real-life scenes from their homes and communities. One child draws a family cooking together, another shows a father helping with homework and another shows friends playing in a clean compound or walking to school. The teacher kneels beside them and asks 'Tell me about your picture', encouraging children to express ideas and stories visually. Some of the finished drawings are displayed on the wall with simple captions using the learners’ own words.

altText: A small group of KG1 children creating one large mural together about their dream school or community.
detailedDescription: On the classroom floor or a wide table, a very large sheet of paper is taped down as a mural space. A small group of KG1 learners works together to create one big picture of their dream school or a healthy community. One child draws buildings, another adds trees and gardens, another draws children learning and playing and another adds bins and water tanks to keep the environment clean. The teacher reminds them to share space and ideas, helping them design, make and respond to an artwork they have created together.

figureLabel: Kente and local patterns as design inspiration
altText: KG1 children studying kente and other local Ghanaian patterns before creating their own simple repeating designs.
detailedDescription: In a KG1 classroom, the teacher shows real kente cloth or large photographs of Ghanaian cloth, baskets and carved doors. Learners point to repeating colours, shapes and symbols and talk briefly about when these items are used in festivals or important events. On the table, strips of paper and crayons are provided so children can design their own simple repeating patterns, for example red–yellow–red–yellow or circle–square–circle–square. The wall displays both the cultural examples and the children’s work, helping learners link Ghanaian art forms with their own creative design.

figureLabel: Recycling art collage from safe materials
altText: KG1 children making collages from clean recycled materials like cardboard, magazine pieces and fabric scraps.
detailedDescription: On a covered table, KG1 children create colourful collages using safe, clean recycled materials such as cardboard, old magazines, fabric scraps, clean bottle caps and string. They glue these onto strong paper to form houses, trees, vehicles or abstract designs. A classroom poster reads 'We don’t waste – we create.' The teacher explains that these materials could have become rubbish but are now used to make something beautiful, building creative confidence and simple problem-solving through making art.

altText: KG1 classroom arranged as a mini-gallery while children present and talk about how they made their artworks.
detailedDescription: The KG1 classroom is arranged as a mini-gallery with drawings, paintings and collages displayed neatly on walls and tables. A small group of children stands at the front; one learner holds up their artwork and explains the materials and steps they used, saying things like 'First I drew my family, then I coloured the clothes.' Classmates listen and ask simple questions and the teacher models helpful comments. The activity trains learners to talk about how they created their artworks and to appreciate others’ efforts.

altText: Ghanaian KG1 children in a circle singing a simple song in call-and-response with their teacher.
detailedDescription: In a Ghanaian KG1 classroom, children sit or stand in a circle while the teacher leads a short, familiar song in call-and-response style. The teacher sings a line such as a greeting or thanks for a new day and the learners joyfully echo it. Some children clap gently on the beat. The scene shows that children can confidently use their voices together to create simple music as part of their everyday learning.

figureLabel: Playing simple rhythm patterns with instruments
altText: KG1 children playing shakers, hand drums and clappers to echo simple rhythm patterns.
detailedDescription: KG1 learners sit or stand holding simple rhythm instruments such as shakers, hand drums and clappers. The teacher demonstrates an easy pattern, for example clap–rest–clap–rest or shake–shake–rest and a small group echoes the same pattern with their instruments. A small wall chart shows simple picture symbols for 'play' and 'rest'. The activity trains careful listening, attention and cooperative rhythm-making as part of creative expression.

altText: KG1 learners using claps, knee taps and gentle stamps to keep a steady beat with a simple rhyme.
detailedDescription: A group of KG1 learners stands in a semi-circle using their bodies as instruments: clapping hands, tapping knees and gently stamping feet to keep a steady beat while the teacher chants a short rhyme. Sometimes a confident child begins the pattern and others follow. The teacher reminds them to listen carefully and stay together, helping them experience that music can be created with the human body without any bought instruments.

figureLabel: Movement to music: fast and slow
altText: KG1 children moving slowly or quickly as music changes tempo, guided by the teacher’s signals.
detailedDescription: In an open space indoors or outside, KG1 children move freely to simple music from a small speaker or the teacher’s clapping. When the music is slow they walk slowly or sway gently; when it becomes fast they make short, quick steps or light jumps. The teacher uses clear hand signals or picture cards for 'slow' and 'fast'. Learners listen and adjust, learning to respond creatively and thoughtfully to changes in tempo.

figureLabel: Simple role-play of home and school scenes
altText: KG1 children acting out simple home and school scenes with basic props while classmates watch.
detailedDescription: Using simple improvised props such as a small bag, book or scarf, KG1 learners act out everyday scenes from home and school. One child plays a parent kindly reminding a child to greet elders, another plays a child going to school and another plays a teacher welcoming learners. Classmates watch and later swap roles. The teacher encourages polite words and respectful gestures, showing that drama can help practise positive behaviour.

altText: KG1 children acting out a short drama where friends quarrel over a toy and then apologise and make peace.
detailedDescription: A small group of KG1 children performs a short drama in which two friends quarrel over a toy and then solve the problem. One child pretends to snatch a toy, another looks upset and a third child suggests sharing or taking turns. The first child apologises and they shake hands or hug. The rest of the class watches while the teacher guides from the side, reinforcing that drama can be used to practise peaceful problem-solving in real life.

figureLabel: Expressing feelings with voice and face
altText: KG1 children taking turns acting out feelings like happy and sad using their faces and voices.
detailedDescription: During circle time, KG1 learners take turns acting out simple feelings such as happy, sad, surprised and afraid. One child shows a happy face and says 'I am happy because I played with my friend', while another shows a sad face and says 'I lost my pencil.' The teacher holds a small chart with drawn faces to help learners name the feelings. The activity uses drama to build emotional vocabulary and empathy.

altText: KG1 children performing a short song or rhyme with actions while classmates and a few parents watch.
detailedDescription: The KG1 classroom is set up for a small performance. A group of children stands at the front singing a short song with actions or reciting a rhyme with simple movements while classmates and a few parents or visitors sit and watch. The song may be a traditional Ghanaian song about greeting, food or festivals. The teacher stands to the side giving quiet support instead of leading. At the end everyone claps, helping learners experience performing for an audience with confidence.

altText: A KG1 classroom with a clearly marked creative arts corner where children freely choose materials and create.
detailedDescription: In a well-organised KG1 classroom, one corner is labelled 'Creative Corner'. Low shelves hold crayons, pencils, papers, safe scissors, glue, boxes of recycled materials and a few simple musical shakers. Two or three children quietly choose materials and begin drawing or constructing while the teacher works with another group. The picture shows that simple tools and materials are always available for learners to handle and explore, not only during a once-a-week art lesson.

figureLabel: Integrating art and maths with shapes and patterns
altText: KG1 children using coloured paper shapes to create pictures and repeating patterns on a table.
detailedDescription: KG1 learners use coloured paper shapes such as circles, triangles and rectangles to build both pictures and repeating patterns. On a low table, one child creates a house and tree from cut-out shapes while another creates a border pattern like circle–triangle–circle–triangle. The teacher points and asks questions such as 'What pattern do you see?' and 'How many circles did you use?', linking the elements of art with early mathematics and design thinking.

altText: KG1 children creating simple drama props from paper and recycled materials before acting out a scene.
detailedDescription: Before a short class drama, KG1 learners work at tables making simple props from paper and recycled materials. Some create paper hats or name tags for characters, others make a pretend shop sign or a cardboard house. Later, a small group uses these props to act out a scene about buying politely at a shop or helping at home. The teacher supports but allows children to decide how to use the props, linking making things with acting out ideas.

figureLabel: Story and art about caring for the environment
altText: KG1 children drawing ways to keep their school and community clean after listening to a story.
detailedDescription: After the teacher reads a short story about keeping the environment clean, KG1 learners sit at tables drawing what they can do to care for their school and community. One child draws a bin with children putting litter inside, another draws classmates watering a tree and another shows someone stopping open burning near the classrooms. The teacher moves around asking 'What is happening in your picture?' linking story, values and visual expression and helping learners see art as part of caring for their environment.

figureLabel: Community project poster: Our caring classroom
altText: KG1 learners designing a large poster about caring behaviours in their classroom.
detailedDescription: On a large sheet of paper titled 'Our Caring Classroom', KG1 learners work together to draw and colour simple rules and caring actions such as sharing materials, helping a friend who falls, sweeping the floor and speaking politely. Some children draw while others help the teacher write short words or labels. The finished poster is meant to be displayed on the wall, encouraging children to see themselves as designers of a caring classroom community.

altText: A KG1 child and teacher looking through a folder of the child’s artworks and discussing a favourite piece.
detailedDescription: In a quiet corner of the KG1 classroom, a child sits with the teacher looking through a simple folder or box of the child’s drawings, paintings and collages. The child points to one artwork and explains why they like it or what they learned from making it. The teacher listens, asks gentle questions and may write a short note. Other portfolios are stacked nearby. The activity helps children talk about their own work, express preferences and see their creative growth over time.
